REL-017.recommendation: Prepare an exit plan for these services, then update B_07.01.0080.
REL-017.expert_advice: The EBA guidelines on outsourcing and Article 28 of DORA require documented and tested exit strategies for these services.

REL-018.message: {count} pair(s) of arrangement and type of service have no rank 1 row in B_05.02.
REL-018.explanation: A rank 1 is expected for each pair (arrangement, ICT service type): it names the direct provider. Exception: an arrangement cited in B_02.03.0020, whose rank 1 is carried by the intra-group arrangement.
REL-018.recommendation: Add the rank 1 row (direct provider, recipient = provider) for each pair listed.
REL-018.expert_advice: A sub-contracted arrangement without rank 1 usually means only the sub-contractors were entered.

REL-019.message: {count} row(s) of B_05.02 break the sub-contracting chain.
REL-019.explanation: A row of rank n >= 2 must name as recipient (B_05.02.0060) a provider of rank n-1 of the same arrangement and service type. Several providers may share a rank (1, 1, 2 is possible). Provisional severity, pending cross-checking with an authority rule.
REL-019.recommendation: Fix the rank or the recipient, or add the missing row of rank n-1.
REL-019.expert_advice: A skipped rank (1 then 3) is the most frequent error.

BUS-018.message: {count} rank 1 row(s) have a recipient different from the provider.
BUS-018.explanation: At rank 1 the recipient of the services (B_05.02.0060 and 0070) is the provider itself (0030 and 0040). Blocking by choice of the project's experts, provisional status: the ITS says the column 'does not apply at the 1st rank' but the EBA key requires a value.
BUS-018.recommendation: Copy the provider's code and type of code to the recipient.
BUS-018.expert_advice: The rank 1 recipient is sometimes the financial entity: the EBA tool expects the provider.

REL-020.message: {count} inconsistency(ies) between the intra-group mechanism of B_02.03 and the intra-group providers of B_01.02.
REL-020.explanation: An arrangement cited in B_02.03.0010 must have an intra-group provider (B_01.02, type x317) at rank 1; a chain going through an intra-group provider must be linked in B_02.03.
REL-020.recommendation: Complete B_02.03 or correct the entity type in B_01.02.
REL-020.expert_advice: B_02.03 prevails for the rank 1 exception (decision P8).

REL-021.message: {count} arrangement(s) linked in B_02.03 have no provider outside the group.
REL-021.explanation: The arrangement linked (B_02.03.0020) to an intra-group arrangement is a contract with a third party: at least one of its providers must be outside the group.
REL-021.recommendation: Identify the first sub-contractor outside the group in B_05.02.
REL-021.expert_advice: A linked arrangement whose providers are all intra-group is a B_02.03 link to review.

BUS-019.message: {count} provider(s) of a chain supporting a critical function have neither a LEI nor an EUID.
BUS-019.explanation: The ITS asks for a LEI or an EUID for legal-person providers; individuals acting in a business capacity are excluded. Provisional severity, pending cross-checking. The validity of the LEI is not checked.
BUS-019.recommendation: Obtain and report the LEI (or EUID) of each provider listed.
BUS-019.expert_advice: Non-EU sub-contractors often have a LEI: ask for it before entering a national code.

DAT-033.message: Table {table}: {count} value(s) of {column} are not among the allowed choices.
DAT-033.explanation: This column only accepts a code from the EBA list (for example eba_GA:FR for France). A label or a misspelt code is not recognised.
DAT-033.recommendation: Replace each value listed under 'Where' by the right code from the list. When the tool suggests a code (arrow), it is the one that matches the value entered.
DAT-033.expert_advice: The error often comes from a label entered instead of the code ('France' instead of eba_GA:FR) or from a tool that changes the case. A currency no longer in use, such as the Croatian kuna (HRK), is not in the list.

DAT-034.message: Table {table}, {column}: {count} natural person(s) declared with an EUID.
DAT-034.explanation: The EUID identifies companies and branches entered in a business register of the Union (Implementing Regulation 2021/1042, annex, point 9). A natural person (B_05.01.0070) cannot have one: either the type of person or the type of code is wrong.
DAT-034.recommendation: If the provider is a company, correct B_05.01.0070 to legal person. Otherwise, report a code suited to a natural person (national code, passport) and correct its type (B_05.01.0020 or B_05.01.0040).
DAT-034.expert_advice: A sole trader entered in a national register has no EUID within the meaning of BRIS: their national number is reported as a company number.

DAT-035.message: Table {table}, {column}: {count} natural person(s) declared with a LEI.
DAT-035.explanation: GLEIF issues LEIs to individuals acting in a business capacity (sole traders), but the case is rare. This finding points to a possible error in the type of person (B_05.01.0070), not to a non-compliance.
DAT-035.recommendation: Check in GLEIF that the LEI belongs to a sole trader. If it is a company, correct B_05.01.0070 to legal person.
DAT-035.expert_advice: A company wrongly reported as a natural person escapes the LEI or EUID check required for legal persons (REL-007, BUS-019): the error in the type of person is worth correcting.

DQ-014.message: {count} provider(s) have a total annual cost lower than the sum of the arrangements that reference them.
DQ-014.explanation: The total annual cost of a provider (B_05.01.0100) should cover at least the annual costs of the arrangements that reference it in B_03.02 (B_02.01.0050). It may be higher, for services outside the register.
DQ-014.recommendation: For each provider listed under 'Where', check its total annual cost and those of its arrangements, and correct the wrong amount.
DQ-014.expert_advice: Information only, with no effect on the score. Overarching arrangements reported at 0 are normal: only subsequent arrangements carry the amounts.

DQ-015.message: {count} arrangement(s) are in another currency than the provider they reference: the amounts were not compared.
DQ-015.explanation: For one arrangement and one provider, the currency of the cost of the arrangement (B_02.01.0040) and that of the total cost of the provider (B_05.01.0090) must be the same. The tool does not convert currencies.
DQ-015.recommendation: Check the currency of each arrangement listed under 'Where' and that of the provider, then report the amounts in the same currency.
DQ-015.expert_advice: Information only, with no effect on the score. As a rule, the reporting currency of the register (B_01.02.0100) is used for every amount.

GLF-001.message: Table {table}, {column}: {count} LEI not found in GLEIF (GLEIF copy of {copy_date}).
GLF-001.explanation: The EBA checks each LEI against the GLEIF database (rule {rule}). These LEI have a correct format but no GLEIF record exists for them: they were mistyped, invented, or belong to an entity that never registered.
GLF-001.recommendation: Look up each value listed under 'Where' on the GLEIF website and copy the exact LEI of the entity. If the entity has no LEI, use another identifier allowed for this column.
GLF-001.expert_advice: EBA warning, no rejection: the register is accepted but the finding comes back in the data quality feedback. A test LEI, valid in format, always ends here.

GLF-002.message: Table {table}, {column}: {count} LEI not valid in GLEIF (GLEIF copy of {copy_date}).
GLF-002.explanation: The register requires a valid and active LEI (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2956, art. 3(5)). In GLEIF these LEI are retired, merged, annulled, duplicates or pending (transfer, archival, validation), or the entity is inactive: they cannot be kept as identifiers.
GLF-002.recommendation: Replace each LEI by the one now in use. When GLEIF gives a successor, it is shown after the arrow under 'Where'.
GLF-002.expert_advice: A merger usually leaves a RETIRED or MERGED LEI pointing to the LEI of the absorbing entity. Check also the contracts: the counterparty may have changed.

GLF-003.message: Table {table}, {column}: {count} LEI not renewed (LAPSED) in GLEIF (GLEIF copy of {copy_date}).
GLF-003.explanation: A LEI must be renewed every year. These LEI still exist but their renewal is overdue: GLEIF shows them as LAPSED. The regulation asks for an active LEI; the ESAs did not enforce the status strictly in 2025 (EBA FAQ, question 44).
GLF-003.recommendation: Ask the entity concerned to renew its LEI with its LEI issuer, or check that you reported the right LEI.
GLF-003.expert_advice: LAPSED does not mean wrong: the identifier stays the same after renewal. Many providers let their LEI lapse; asking them early avoids a finding the year enforcement is tightened.

GLF-004.message: Table {table}, {column}: {count} LEI to be renewed before {deadline} (GLEIF copy of {copy_date}).
GLF-004.explanation: These LEI are valid today, but their renewal date falls before the probable end of the processing of the register by the EBA (30 April after the reference date). The EBA checks the LEI when it processes the register, not at the reference date: a LEI not renewed by then will be LAPSED.
GLF-004.recommendation: Remind the entities concerned to renew their LEI before the date shown under 'Where'.
GLF-004.expert_advice: Information only. The date of 30 April is an estimate: the EBA ran its data quality checks in April in 2026.

GLF-005.message: Table {table}, {column}: the country of {count} entity(ies) differs from GLEIF (GLEIF copy of {copy_date}).
GLF-005.explanation: The EBA compares the country of each entity of B_01.02 with GLEIF (rule {rule}). The country reported is neither the country of the legal address nor that of the headquarters recorded in GLEIF.
GLF-005.recommendation: Check the country of the entity and correct either the register or the GLEIF record (through the LEI issuer).
GLF-005.expert_advice: EBA warning, no rejection. The EBA does not say which GLEIF address it uses: this check accepts either the legal address or the headquarters.

GLF-006.message: Table {table}, {column}: the country of {count} entity(ies) differs from GLEIF (GLEIF copy of {copy_date}).
GLF-006.explanation: The country reported is neither the country of the legal address nor that of the headquarters recorded in GLEIF for the same LEI.
GLF-006.recommendation: Check the country of the entity and correct the register if needed.
GLF-006.expert_advice: Not an EBA rule: a consistency check of this product. A provider whose GLEIF record is outdated can also explain the difference.

GLF-007.message: Table {table}, {column}: the name of {count} entity(ies) differs from the GLEIF legal name (GLEIF copy of {copy_date}).
GLF-007.explanation: The name reported does not resemble the legal name recorded in GLEIF for the same LEI, even after removing case, accents and punctuation. The LEI may belong to another entity.
GLF-007.recommendation: Compare the names listed under 'Where' with GLEIF: correct the LEI if it is not the right entity, or the name otherwise.
GLF-007.expert_advice: A trade name, an old name or a name in another alphabet can explain the difference. When the LEI is wrong, the whole row describes the wrong company.

GLF-008.message: Table {table}, {column}: the direct parent of {count} entity(ies) differs from GLEIF (GLEIF copy of {copy_date}).
GLF-008.explanation: The LEI of the direct parent reported in B_01.02.0060 is not the direct accounting consolidating parent recorded in GLEIF.
GLF-008.recommendation: Check the group structure and correct the register, or ask the entity to update its parent in GLEIF.
GLF-008.expert_advice: GLEIF records accounting consolidation parents, reported by the entities themselves: a recent reorganisation may not be there yet.

GLF-009.message: Table {table}, {column}: the ultimate parent of {count} provider(s) differs from GLEIF (GLEIF copy of {copy_date}).
GLF-009.explanation: For every provider identified by a LEI, the ultimate parent reported in B_05.01.0110 must be the ultimate accounting consolidating parent recorded in GLEIF. Here it is different, empty (∅), or identified otherwise than by a LEI (type in brackets).
GLF-009.recommendation: Report in B_05.01.0110 the LEI of the ultimate parent given by GLEIF (after 'GLEIF' under 'Where'), with the type LEI in B_05.01.0120.
GLF-009.expert_advice: Useful for concentration: a wrong ultimate parent splits a group into several providers in the supervisors' view.

GLF-010.message: GLEIF checks not performed: no GLEIF copy is installed.
GLF-010.explanation: The LEI are checked against a local copy of the GLEIF data, downloaded when the tool starts. No copy could be installed (no network or no access to the repository): the GLEIF checks are shown as not evaluated.
GLF-010.recommendation: Restart the tool with an internet connection, and check the access to the repository (ROI_GLEIF_TOKEN) if it is private.
GLF-010.expert_advice: The rest of the analysis is complete: only the GLEIF comparisons are missing.

GLF-011.explanation: The GLEIF checks used a copy published {days} days ago. A LEI may have lapsed or been retired since.
GLF-011.recommendation: Restart the tool with an internet connection to download the latest copy, then analyse the register again.
GLF-011.expert_advice: GLEIF publishes its files several times a day; the copy is refreshed when a new release is published on the repository.
